ai.title: Static gpt-4o encoder in token-counter
ai.summary: Backend token-counter.ts initializes encoder once for gpt-4o-2024-08-06 instead of per-call. Removed TiktokenModel param from countTokens and countTokensForFiles. Eliminates repeated allocation and free() overhead.

eli5.text: The system now loads its text-measuring tool once at startup instead of setting it up and tearing it down every single time it needs to count words, which reduces wasted work behind the scenes. This affects anyone using the platform's token counting features internally, and you would notice faster, more efficient processing without any visible change to what the tools output. The change is live today and trims unnecessary steps from a backend utility.

ai.title: Add manifold mock project to backend test fixtures
ai.summary: Full Manifold Markets monorepo snapshot added under backend/src/__tests__/__mock-projects__/manifold/ as a test fixture. Provides a realistic multi-package codebase (web/, backend/, common/, docs/) with Firebase, Supabase, Vercel, Docker, and ESLint configs for exercising backend parsing and analysis paths. Scope limited to backend test infrastructure; no runtime or user-facing surface affected. 196,586 lines added across the fixture tree.

eli5.text: The company's own programmers added a complete, realistic copy of the Manifold Markets website's internal code into their testing area. This fake copy includes all the configuration files for their hosting, databases, and code-checking tools, so when they run their automated tests, those tests can practice working with code that looks just like their real, messy production system instead of simple fake examples. Your experience as a user does not change at all because this copy only lives inside their testing system. You can tell this is test-only because everything is tucked away under a 'test mock projects' folder, and the programmers explicitly said it only affects their backend testing infrastructure, not the live website you use.

ai.title: Refactor applyChanges to common/util/changes and switch tests to bun
ai.summary: applyChanges and getProjectFileTree moved from npm-app/src/project-files.ts to new common modules (util/changes.ts, project-file-tree.ts). CLI and client now import from common, passing projectRoot explicitly. Backend test runner switched from jest to bun test; jest/ts-jest deps removed. New manifold-project.test.ts added.

eli5.text: The team moved the assistant's file-editing and project-scanning tools into a shared module so the chat app and the command-line tool can both use the same code without duplicating it. When the assistant applies your code changes, it now writes them based on a project folder you specify explicitly instead of guessing, which makes editing more reliable. Behind the scenes, the test suite that guards this behavior switched from Jest to Bun, which means the checks run a bit faster, but you wouldn't see that directly unless you were running the tests yourself.

ai.title: Add score-tests helper for manifold project tests
ai.summary: New `score-tests.ts` helper implements `projectTest` to track pass/fail counts via `expectTrue` callbacks. `manifold-project.test.ts` refactored to use this helper, replacing direct `expect` calls with scored assertions. This internal change improves test observability by logging individual check results and a final score ratio.

eli5.text: The developers who build and verify the software's correctness now have a new scoreboard for their tests. When they run checks to confirm a feature works, each individual check is counted, labeled as passed or failed, and they see a final tally like '7 out of 10 checks passed' instead of just a simple pass/fail for the whole group of tests. This is purely a tool for the builders to get a clearer picture of what's working, and it doesn't change anything you would experience when using the application.

ai.title: Add incrementScore to projectTest for granular type error scoring
ai.summary: Refactored `projectTest` in `backend/src/__tests__/score-tests.ts` to expose an `incrementScore` callback alongside `expectTrue`. The manifold test in `backend/src/__tests__/manifold-project.test.ts` now parses `tsc` output to count files with type errors, awarding points proportionally instead of binary pass/fail. This enables granular scoring for compilation success in agent evaluations.

eli5.text: The automated system that checks whether an AI assistant correctly edits code now gives partial credit instead of just pass or fail. When the assistant's code has type errors, it awards points based on how many of the affected files were fixed correctly, so a mostly-right answer scores higher than a fully-broken one. This only affects the internal evaluation process that measures AI performance; you would see more detailed score breakdowns in test logs rather than an all-or-nothing result.
